entities.name: PMID:27399746
observations: Cross-sectional FIFA 11+ study in 12 youth soccer teams found 90% of coaches expected injury-risk reduction but reported limited intention to use the program; no subsequent delivery was measured.
Player task self-efficacy predicted implementation intention (β=0.53, p≤0.01), while risk perception did not (β=−0.02).

entities.name: PMID:23486935
observations: Prospective 4-month FIFA 11+ trial in 31 Canadian female youth football teams recorded actual delivery but not a validated preseason coach-intention measure.
Session completion was 85.6% with workshop plus supervision, 81.3% with workshop alone, and 73.5% with website-only delivery; adjusted differences were not statistically significant.

entities.name: PMID:34213586
observations: Prospective Knee Control cohort found high-compliance teams averaged 95% compliance versus 50% in low-compliance teams, with weekly doses of 2.4, 1.4, and 0.7 sessions across high-, intermediate-, and low-dose groups.

High- and low-compliance teams did not differ in baseline coach prevention expectancies, indicating baseline attitudes did not distinguish later implementation; high-compliance teams had better utilization fidelity.

entities.name: PMID:34501680
observations: An ACL neuromuscular-training education RCT improved perceived implementation feasibility but did not measure later field delivery, dose, adherence, fidelity, or player exposure.
Among 256 participants, animated video comprehension effect size was d=0.86 versus d=0.39 for text; active groups had higher feasibility ratings than placebo (p=0.01).

entities.name: Coach intention–implementation evidence
observations: Direct longitudinal evidence that high coach intention predicts ACL-prevention implementation is sparse.
The direct FIFA 11+ intention study was cross-sectional, and prospective FIFA 11+ and Knee Control studies measured delivery/compliance without a validated pre-season intention construct.

Knee Control baseline prevention expectancies did not distinguish high- from low-compliance teams, providing evidence against assuming that favorable coach attitudes reliably translate into implementation.
